binaries.name: fsapfsinfo
binaries.why: Read an APFS container and its volumes, snapshots included, which the Sleuth Kit does not.

binaries.name: log
binaries.why: Apple's own reader for the unified log. Only present on macOS, and the only tool that resolves the format strings properly.

install.apt: not available on Linux; use UnifiedLogReader

binaries.not_in_image: Apple's own reader exists only on macOS, so no Linux image can hold it; UnifiedLogReader.py reads the same archives there.

binaries.name: mac_apt.py
binaries.why: Fifty-odd artefact plugins over a macOS or iOS image, and it reads UAC and Velociraptor collections as well as E01, DMG and sparse images.

install.apt: pinned source 1.33.2 (install.source), amd64 only: its statx helper knows no aarch64 syscall number, so it stops at import on Linux arm64

binaries.name: UnifiedLogReader.py
binaries.why: Read a unified log archive on a host that is not a Mac, where Apple's own log command does not exist.

install.brew: https://github.com/ydkhatri/UnifiedLogReader (run scripts/UnifiedLogReader.py from a clone, with biplist and lz4 installed: PyPI has no UnifiedLogReader project, and its UnifiedLog 0.3 does not build with pip 20 or later)
install.apt: pinned source 20200124 (install.source): PyPI has no UnifiedLogReader project, and its UnifiedLog 0.3 does not build with pip 20 or later, so the script runs from the checkout
